To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the achievable rates of power-constrained wide-band relay networks with AF relaying and network training are characterized by the following scaling laws, which hold for both the narrowband regime and the wideband regime.

for a wireless sensory relay network, the scaling law can always be achieved by using the simple equal power allocation scheme across the frequency sub-bands at the relay nodes, provided that the transmission energy per fading block is bounded from below.

the achievable rates of power-constrained narrowband and wideband relay networks have the same scaling order with respect to the system parameters, and that the corresponding scaling laws can be characterized by using AF with a simple network training scheme.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a unified framework for the analysis of achievable rates of wireless relay networks, and identify conditions under which the achievable rates scale as a function of the number of relays and the bandwidth.
the relay networks can achieve the same scaling law as in coherent relay networks, provided that the energy per fading blocks per subband is bounded below, which is a very mild assumption.

the achievable rates of power-constrained relay networks in both narrowband and wideband scenarios can be characterized by the scaling law in the joint asymptotics of n, L, and W, and this scaling law is independent of the channel coherence interval, the channel bandwidth, and the number of relay users.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the considered relay network model, AF with network training achieves the same scaling laws as coherent relaying, and the network training overhead is not a major concern in the wideband relay network design.

, in the low SNRs, the achievable rates by AF with network training can approach the optimal scaling laws, and thus AF with network training is capable of providing the same scaling laws as coherent relaying.

the scaling laws of the power-constrained wide-band relay networks are independent of the power allocation policies, as long as L is bounded below, which is in sharp contrast to the case of narrowband relay networks where the power allocation policy plays an important role in the achievable rate.
